name: Seventh-day Adventist Church

facts.value: Formed into a body by 1845, emerging from the Millerite movement after 1844

citations.excerpt: They were formed into a body in 1845.

disagreements.excerpt: Seventh-day Adventist Church (1844 - Present) - Religious Group

citations.excerpt: The Seventh-day Adventist Church grew out of the work of William Miller, who predicted the Second Coming of Christ in 1843/44.

facts.value: Ellen G. White and James White

citations.excerpt: Some who continued as Adventists and also accepted sabbath worship found new leadership in the persons of Ellen G. White and James White.

facts.value: Seventh-day Sabbath, the dead unconscious until judgment, and the prophetic gift as held by Ellen G. White.

citations.excerpt: These hold to the observance of the seventh day of the week as the Sabbath . They believe that the dead remain unconscious until Judgment , when the wicked will be destroyed.
believe the prophetic gift is still communicated, and was possessed latterly by Mrs. E.G. White in particular.
